Stellenbosch FC have completed three more signings before the start of the 2026/27 Betway Premiership season.

The Winelands club announced the arrivals of George Matlou, Terrence Mashego, and Nathan Garrow. All three players strengthen different areas of the squad.

ROB BENADIE WELCOMES NEW SIGNINGS

Matlou, 28, joins Stellenbosch FC on a free transfer. The former Kaizer Chiefs midfielder signed a long-term contract after leaving Amakhosi.

“George is a player we believe can add real value to our squad through his experience, technical ability, and understanding of the game,” Stellenbosch FC CEO Rob Benadie said.



“His pedigree speaks for itself, and we are naturally pleased that he has chosen to continue his career with Stellenbosch FC. We believe he can play an important role in helping us achieve our objectives this season.”

Also read: Latest report: Kaizer Chiefs offer more money for Stellenbosch star

Mashego also joins the club. The Bafana Bafana left-back arrives on a season-long loan from Mamelodi Sundowns. He adds quality and experience to the defence.



“Terrence is a player who has competed at the highest level on both the domestic and international stages, and we believe he has the ability and quality to add significant value to our squad,” Stellenbosch FC CEO Rob Benadie said. “We are delighted to welcome him to the Club.”

STELLENBOSCH FC ADD DEPTH

The club also completed the permanent signing of goalkeeper Nathan Garrow from New Zealand side Auckland City.

The goalkeeper will compete for a place in the first-team squad. His arrival gives the club more depth between the posts.



Stellenbosch FC CEO, Rob Benadie, said, “We are delighted to welcome Nathan to Stellenbosch FC. He is a talented young goalkeeper with outstanding potential, and his performances over the past year have demonstrated that he has the quality to succeed at a high level.

“He has an incredibly bright future ahead of him, and we believe that he will benefit from the opportunities for growth that exist at the Club, while simultaneously helping to improve our goalkeeping department.”

These signings continue Stellenbosch FC’s busy transfer window. The club recently secured Thabiso Lebitso from Orlando Pirates and midfielder Sinoxolo Kwayiba on permanent deals.



The latest arrivals show the club’s ambition. The Maroons want to compete strongly in the Betway Premiership and other competitions this season.

World.title: Anele Tembe ‘evidence’: What really happened at the Hilton Hotel?
World.content:
Anele Tembe reportedly attempted suicide at the Hilton hotel in 2020. Images via X

Tony Forbes – the father of the late rapper AKA, or Kiernan Forbes – has admitted to releasing “evidence” suggesting that Anele Tembe was suicidal and took her own life in 2021. Forbes has referenced a previous suicide attempt at the Hilton Hotel just months earlier.

Anele fell to her death off the 10th floor of the Pepperclub Hotel balcony after a heated argument with her fiancé.

Up until his own death in 2023, AKA denied any involvement.



On Monday, 13 July, the inquest into Anele’s death was postponed to September.

TONY FORBES RELEASES ‘EVIDENCE’ CLAIMING ANELE TEMBE WAS SUICIDAL

In a statement posted on his Instagram account, Tony Forbes admitted to leaking screenshots of WhatsApp messages between AKA and Anele Tembe, as well as the Tembe family lawyer.

In it, AKA texted the attorney about Anele’s threats to jump off the roof of the Hilton Hotel after an argument.

Anele threatened that “next time”, she would follow through with her threat, in another text.

A third message showed that Anele’s father, businessman Moses Tembe, called out his daughter as a “talented and dramatic actress”.

Shocking 😮



AKA and the Tembe family lawyer exchanged WhatsApp texts messages regarding the initial incident in which Anele Tembe made a threat to jump from a building.



2. Anele Tembe discusses suicide in a text message with AKA. pic.twitter.com/qR5HLAiMvC  July 13, 2026

Forbes said of his actions: “I did it as his father….I could not save him, but I can fight for his name and memory”.

Forbes stated he felt compelled to act over the “character assassination” of his son, claiming that the “time was right to put this information into the public domain to bring balance, to bring fact. Not speculatiaon. Not to create a false narrative”.

Tony Forbes claimed that the texts had supported the National Prosecuting Authority’s decision that there was no foul play in the death of Anele Tembe.

Forbes also accused the police investigating officer of negligence for not including the texts in the case docket.

He added: “Read the texts and decide for yourself”.

WHAT HAPPENED AT THE HILTON HOTEL?

In December 2020, Anele Tembe made headlines after she attempted to jump off the top of the 19-storey Hilton Hotel.

According to TimesLive, Anele had stood on the ledge of the top floor in the early morning. An unidentified female cousin reportedly tried to talk her off the ledge.

The publication claimed that Anele was “highly aggressive” when approached by authorities. Eventually, she was distracted and pulled off the ledge.

The 22-year-old was later taken to a nearby medical centre for treatment. She would also undergo counselling at the Akeso Umhlanga clinic, a psychiatric hospital for people with mental health issues.

AKA & Anele Tembe's relationship was toxic,I always had a icky feeling about him wanting to marry such a young girl. But trying to say he killed her,when this girl tried jumping of the Hilton hotel in Durban https://t.co/XqU9kSi3fi why doesn't anyone mention her attempted suicide pic.twitter.com/gvuIGbrg9H — TheClrdChicka (@clrd_the) February 16, 2023

Speaking in an interview with author Melinda Ferguson in her book When Love Kills: The Tragic Tale of AKA and Anele, Moses Tembe rubbished reports that his daughter wanted to jump off the Hilton Hotel.

He said, “I don’t know what led to her standing up there. It was not something that my daughter would have done. I do not believe Anele was going to jump. My daughter loved herself so much. Anele was a very dramatic girl. She loved attention”.

AKA AND ANELE TEMBE: ANOTHER EXPLOSIVE

According to Melinda Ferguson, Anele Tembe had stormed the Hilton in Durban on the morning of 11 December 2020 to look for AKA, who had been a guest of the five-star hotel.

AKA had attended the launch of his restaurant and bar, Cuba BLK, just a day earlier, claimed IOL.

After she was unable to locate him, Anele allegedly took the lift up to the 19th floor, where she climbed the ledge and threatened to jump.

According to the author, Anele suspected AKA of cheating on her and hoped to confront him.

World.title: Pensioner’s R2 400 SASSA grant breakdown leaves just R400 for food
World.content:
A line-by-line budget shared in the Facebook comments of a recent SASSA pensioner story by The South African has laid bare how little of the R2 400 Older Persons Grant remains once basic costs are covered.

Commenter Karen Grebe posted a breakdown for a pensioner she referred to as “Old David,” showing rent at R800, a monthly hospital trip at R300, and R600 spent on medicine bought from a private pharmacy because the local hospital was non-existent. Toilet paper, cleaning products, toothpaste and soap added a further R300 to the total.

Once those costs were subtracted from the R2 400 grant, only R400 remained for food for the entire month, according to Grebe’s calculation.



Other pensioners describe similar struggles

The breakdown struck a chord with other commenters. Marthie Diedericks responded that no human being can survive on that amount. Tenane Sophie Seema, describing her own situation as a pensioner, said there is no way a human being can live with R2 400 monthly.

Commenter Rina Nel, who said she is 82 years old and receives the old-age pension, shared that she worked from age 16 until 70 and received no pension from her former employer. She now relies on a small pension from her late husband, who passed away three years ago. Nel said her unemployed son, who has been out of work for over 11 years despite being highly qualified, depends on her, as does her daughter. She said she had to cancel her medical aid entirely due to the cost.

Rising costs squeeze grants further

These accounts illustrate a pattern raised repeatedly in the comments: fixed grant amounts failing to keep pace with the real cost of rent, healthcare and daily essentials. With food prices and medical costs continuing to climb, pensioners relying solely on the Older Persons Grant say the shortfall is forcing impossible monthly trade-offs between medicine, hygiene products and food.

World.title: 7 of the most charming main streets in South Africa
World.content:
Some towns are famous for a landmark or a scenic viewpoint. Others are remembered for something much simpler: their main street.

It’s where locals greet each other by name, cafés spill onto the pavement, antique shops tempt passers-by, and historic buildings tell stories stretching back generations.

The best main streets invite you to slow down. You park the car, wander without a plan and somehow spend far longer there than you intended.

Here are some of South Africa’s most charming main streets.



1. Greyton

Greyton, Western Cape. Image: canva

Greyton’s oak-lined streets are among the prettiest in the country.

Instead of traffic lights and shopping centres, you’ll find heritage cottages, garden gates overflowing with roses, artisan bakeries and independent cafés.

On Saturday mornings, the village market adds even more life to the town, while the surrounding mountains provide a spectacular backdrop that changes with the seasons.



Greyton’s main street is the kind of place where a quick coffee stop easily turns into an entire afternoon.

2. Clarens

Clarens revolves around its lively town square, where galleries, restaurants and craft shops line the streets beneath dramatic sandstone mountains.

Artists display their work, outdoor tables fill with visitors, and every direction offers another beautiful mountain view.



Whether you’re browsing local galleries or simply enjoying lunch in the sunshine, the town’s relaxed atmosphere makes it one of South Africa’s most enjoyable places for a leisurely stroll.

3. Cullinan

Cullinan, Gauteng. Image: wikimedia commons

Cullinan’s historic heart feels remarkably untouched.

Its wide streets are lined with beautifully preserved sandstone buildings dating back to the town’s diamond-mining boom, alongside antique shops, coffee houses and boutique stores.



There’s a timeless quality here that’s increasingly rare, making it one of Gauteng’s best destinations for a relaxed weekend outing.

4. Stellenbosch

Few streets in South Africa are as recognisable as Stellenbosch’s historic centre.

Shaded by giant oak trees, the town’s main streets combine elegant Cape Dutch architecture with bustling cafés, wine bars, bookstores and galleries.



Students, tourists and locals create a lively atmosphere throughout the year, while the surrounding mountains complete one of the country’s most beautiful urban landscapes.

5. Prince Albert

Dutch Reformed Church in Prince Albert, Western Cape. Image: wikimedia commons

Prince Albert’s main street captures everything people love about the Karoo.

Historic cottages, galleries, delis and cafés sit against the dramatic backdrop of the Swartberg Mountains, creating a village that’s both peaceful and sophisticated.



It’s a place where visitors naturally slow their pace, whether they’re stopping for homemade ice cream or browsing handcrafted goods.

6. Rosendal

Rosendal may be small, but its main street has enormous charm.

Surrounded by rolling farmland and sandstone mountains, the village is known for its art galleries, cafés and beautifully restored historic buildings.



It’s the sort of place where you arrive intending to stretch your legs for ten minutes and end up staying the night.

7. McGregor

Quiet, artistic and wonderfully unhurried, McGregor’s main street is lined with whitewashed cottages, galleries, vineyards and welcoming cafés.

There are no crowds or towering buildings here, just wide streets, mountain views and a pace of life that encourages visitors to linger a little longer.



The town has become a favourite among artists and creatives, and that relaxed character is evident around every corner.

World.title: Exclusive: Q&A with Linda Mtoba after ‘Masked Singer SA’ exit
World.content:
South African actress and media personality Linda Mtoba was revealed to be the face behind the mask of Lady Monster on the lastest episode of The Masked Singer South Africa Season three, which aired on SABC2 on Saturday 11 July.

LINDA MTOBA UNDER THE MASK OF LADY MONSTER

Lady Monster had the panel of detectives completely fooled on the latest episode of The Masked Singer South Africa Season three. Somizi Mhlongo, J’Something, Sithelo Shozi, and Skhumba all failed to identify her behind the fluffy costume, despite chasing clues in her song choice, movements, and introduction package. Lady Monster performed the lively hit Golden by HUNTR/X but lost her round against Mosquito, landing in the danger zone alongside Spotty.

Her clue package hinted at her rise to fame in 2016, the year Pokémon Go became popular, and included playful references to cooking without recipes and rejecting comic-book saviours. These clues sent the panel in different directions, with guesses ranging from Mampho Brescia to Busiswa Gqulu, Thembi Seete, and Brenda Ngxoli. Even Sithelo, who is close friends with Linda, was misled, believing Lady Monster was another actress.

When Linda finally unmasked herself, the detectives were stunned, especially Sithelo, who shouted about Linda’s daughter Beanie, a big fan of the show. Linda admitted that her family will tease her for months for keeping her identity secret. Known for her breakout role in Isibaya in 2016, Linda has since become a household name and style icon in South Africa.



The Masked Singer South Africa Season three is produced by Rose and Oaks Media for Primedia Studios, the show airs on SABC 2 on Saturdays at 19:00, with rebroadcasts on SABC 1 on Thursdays at 21:00 and SABC 2 on Fridays at 13:30. The episodes are also available on Netflix.

In the previous episode, comedian Trevor Gumbi was revealed as Ponte Tower.

Q&A WITH LINDA MTOBA

What made you choose Lady Monster?



I chose Lady Monster because she’s a lady and she’s a monster like me. She is pink, she’s got beat, she is absolutely fabolous. So, it was a no-brainer for me honestly. I loved the costume.

Was it difficult keeping the secret from your friends and family?

It was difficult keeping the secret because all of a sudden everyone becomes detectives at home asking me why do I have pink fluff on myself, what was I doing today at work, so it becomes kind of a difficult one to navigate. All of a sudden everyone is curious about my day at the office.



How did your family react to finding our you were Lady Monster?

They were so chuffed, so surprised and so happy because we love watching it and it was such a pleasure to actually see me on stages and see their faces. They are very, very happy and excited for it. The whole family enjoyed it.

World.title: Devastating news for Cape Town ice cream lovers as beloved chain closes
World.content:
Beloved Cape Town ice cream brand The Creamery is set to close all of its remaining stores, bringing an end to a 15-year journey. Image: Instagram @thecreamerysa

Beloved Cape Town ice cream brand The Creamery is set to close all of its remaining stores, bringing an end to a 15-year journey that saw it grow from a market stall favourite into one of the city’s best-known artisanal brands.

Food Lover’s Market, through its subsidiary Seattle Coffee Company, confirmed that The Creamery’s four remaining outlets will shut their doors in the coming weeks.

The closures affect stores in Mouille Point, Durbanville, Palmyra Junction and Newlands.

The brand’s Constantia Emporium branch had already closed in February 2023.



READ | Iconic Newlands Chinese eatery closes its restaurant after 44 years

Staff told The South African that they were largely in the dark when it came to the reasons for the closure, saying “we have no idea” and “that’s what the bosses decided”.

The South African has established that the Palmyra Junction store will close on Sunday, 19 July while the other three branches will close their doors on Sunday, 16 August.



From market favourite to household name

The Creamery was founded in 2011 by former chef Kate Schrire and business partner Marianne Visser.

Built on a philosophy of using local, seasonal ingredients, the business first gained a loyal following by selling handcrafted ice cream at Cape Town markets and festivals before opening its first permanent store on Dean Street in Newlands in 2013.

The company later expanded its retail footprint while operating a production facility in Salt River.



Its flavours and emphasis on high-quality ingredients helped establish The Creamery as one of South Africa’s leading artisanal ice cream brands.

Covid acquisition

Seattle Coffee Company acquired The Creamery during the Covid-19 pandemic after the business faced severe trading challenges.

At the time, the company said the previous owners had been navigating an exceptionally difficult retail environment brought about by the pandemic.



Schrire remained involved with the business until 2023. At one stage, The Creamery employed around 65 people.

Stores to close gradually

According to notices displayed in stores, the remaining outlets will close on different dates rather than all at once, giving loyal customers a final opportunity to visit before trading ends.

Neither Food Lover’s Market nor Seattle Coffee Company has publicly disclosed the reasons behind the decision to close the remaining stores.



Customer reaction

Reaction to the news was met with widespread disbelief.

Sarah Jacobs, Newlands: “It’s heartbreaking. The Creamery was part of so many family outings over the years. My kids grew up choosing a different flavour every weekend, and it won’t feel the same without it.”

Michael Petersen, Durbanville: “I remember queuing outside the Newlands store after rugby matches. Their ice cream wasn’t cheap, but it always felt like a treat worth paying for.”



Lebo Mokoena, Cape Town: “Cape Town is losing another local institution. The Creamery wasn’t just about ice cream—it was part of the city’s food culture.”

Ayesha Daniels, Mouille Point: “I’m sad to see another South African success story disappear. It feels like the end of an era for artisanal ice cream in Cape Town.”

Jason Williams, Claremont: “I’ll definitely be making one last trip before my local branch closes. There are some flavours you just can’t replace.”



Nadine Smith, Rondebosch: “It’s a reminder of how difficult the retail and hospitality industries have become. I just hope the staff are able to find new opportunities soon.”

The closure marks the end of a chapter for a brand that became synonymous with premium ice cream in Cape Town, leaving many customers nostalgic for a business that helped shape the city’s artisanal food scene over the past decade and a half.

World.title: eMedia Launches Openview Stream, Africa’s First Independent FAST Streaming Platform
World.content:
Johannesburg, South Africa | 13 July 2026 – eMedia, one of Africa’s leading entertainment businesses, today announced the launch of Openview Stream, Africa’s first independent Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) platform. As an eMedia platform, Openview Stream extends the group’s entertainment ecosystem beyond traditional broadcasting, delivering premium live television and streaming content free to audiences across Africa.

Building on the established Openview brand, which has transformed free television access for millions of households in South Africa, Openview Stream marks the next evolution of eMedia’s media portfolio by extending that familiar viewing experience into digital streaming across Africa.

Developed in partnership with RunnTV, eMedia’s strategic OTT and FAST technology partner, Openview Stream combines eMedia’s recognised entertainment brands, quality content and deep understanding of African audiences with world-class FAST capability to create a seamless streaming experience designed specifically for the continent.

The platform launches initially across Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, Zambia, Botswana, Namibia and Mauritius, with additional African markets planned as part of eMedia’s phased expansion strategy.

Building on decades of delivering quality entertainment to millions of households, eMedia is expanding into the streaming market with Openview Stream. The service creates new opportunities for local authorities, broadcasters, audiences, advertisers and content creators by providing a sustainable, advertising-supported digital ecosystem tailored to African viewing habits.

As an eMedia platform, Openview Stream also supports the continued growth of Africa’s broadcasting industry by providing broadcasters and content owners with an innovative digital distribution service. Through RunnTV’s proven FAST technology, partners can extend their reach across mobile devices and Connected TVs while creating new opportunities to grow audiences and unlock sustainable advertising revenue.

Africa is one of the world’s fastest-growing digital entertainment markets. Increasing smart television adoption, improved broadband connectivity and growing demand for free streaming services are changing how audiences discover and consume content. Openview Stream has been developed to meet this demand by delivering an accessible, high-quality streaming destination that remains free to viewers.

The platform offers a carefully curated mix of African, regional and international channels, with programming focused on local relevance, established entertainment brands and high-quality viewing experiences that reflect the diversity of audiences across the continent.

Commenting on the launch, Khalik Sherrif, CEO of eMedia, said:

“Openview Stream represents another important milestone in eMedia’s evolution as one of Africa’s leading entertainment businesses. Building on the success of Openview, we are extending one of our strongest consumer brands into the streaming market, ensuring audiences can continue to enjoy quality entertainment through a free, accessible viewing experience. Together with RunnTV, our strategic technology partner, we are creating an African streaming service that delivers value for viewers, broadcasters, advertisers and content creators while making premium entertainment freely accessible across the continent.”

Manish Sinha, Founder and CEO of RunnTV, added:

“Africa represents one of the most exciting growth markets for the future of television. We are proud to partner with eMedia to power Openview Stream through our FAST technology platform. By combining eMedia’s established brands and deep market expertise with our technology capabilities, we are creating a scalable streaming service designed specifically for African audiences.”

The launch marks another important step in eMedia’s long-term digital growth strategy. Over the coming months, Openview Stream will continue to expand its content offering, channel portfolio, and geographic footprint, strengthening its position as Africa’s leading independent FAST streaming destination.

About Openview Stream

Openview Stream is an eMedia platform and Africa’s first independent Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) service. Building on the established Openview brand, the service extends eMedia’s media portfolio into digital streaming, delivering live television and curated entertainment through a free, advertising-supported experience. Developed with RunnTV as eMedia’s strategic FAST technology partner, Openview Stream launches across seven African countries, with additional markets planned as part of its continental expansion strategy.

About eMedia

eMedia is one of Africa’s leading entertainment businesses, connecting millions of viewers through a diverse portfolio of broadcast, satellite, streaming and digital platforms. Its portfolio includes e.tv, South Africa’s free-to-air television broadcaster; Openview, South Africa’s leading free satellite television platform; Openview Stream, the group’s Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) platform; eVOD, its premium streaming service; and eNCA, one of Africa’s leading 24-hour news channels.

About RunnTV

RunnTV is a leading FAST streaming technology company focused on building the future of free television. Through its proprietary FAST technology platform, RunnTV enables broadcasters and media companies to create, distribute and monetise premium streaming experiences across Connected TV and digital ecosystems globally.

**ENDS**
